$$f(r):=1-\frac{2M}{r}+\frac{Q^2}{r^2}\ne0\qquad(r\in J).$$
On the smooth product $\mathcal M_J:=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times J_r\times S^2$,
use $S^2=\{(X,Y,Z)\in\mathbb R^3:X^2+Y^2+Z^2=1\}$ with its subspace
topology ([[def-euclidean-spheres-and-closed-balls]]). Specify the smooth
structure by the sphere atlas of [[def-gr-schwarzschild-exterior-model]],
Definition (b): for $\varepsilon=\pm1$, delete $p_\varepsilon=(0,0,\varepsilon)$
and use $\sigma_\varepsilon(X,Y,Z)=(X,Y)/(1-\varepsilon Z)$.
For $u=(u_1,u_2)$ and $h=u_1^2+u_2^2$, its inverse is

the transition is $u\mapsto u/h$ on $h>0$. These rational maps are smooth
on their domains. The product atlas consists of

$\mathbb R\times J\times(S^2\setminus\{p_\varepsilon\})$;

The product is Hausdorff and second countable by the subspace topology from
$\mathbb R^2\times\mathbb R^3$, whose rational balls give a countable basis.
These charts specify its maximal smooth atlas, including when $J$ is empty.
The inclusion of $S^2$ into $\mathbb R^3$ is smooth with injective differential
in these parametrizations; its induced unit round metric is $\gamma_{S^2}$
([[ex-the-round-metric-on-the-sphere-as-an-induced-metric]]).
Orient $S^2$ by its outward unit normal: for $p\in S^2$ and
$u,v\in T_pS^2$, define
$$ (\omega_{S^2})_p(u,v):=\det(p,u,v). $$
Thus $\omega_{S^2}$ is the positive area form of $\gamma_{S^2}$, and in the
polar chart $X=\sin\theta\cos\phi$, $Y=\sin\theta\sin\phi$,
$Z=\cos\theta$ it is $\sin\theta\,d\theta\wedge d\phi$. The **dyonic RN
datum** is
$$g=-f(r)\,dx^0\otimes dx^0+f(r)^{-1}\,dr\otimes dr+r^2\gamma_{S^2}, \qquad \mathcal F=-\frac{q_e}{r^2}\,dx^0\wedge dr+q_m\omega_{S^2}.$$
Here $x^0$ and $r$ have units of metres, angles on $S^2$ are dimensionless,
and $M,q_e,q_m$ have units of metres. The metric components are dimensionless
in length coordinates; the nonzero coordinate components of $\mathcal F$ have
units inherited from their coordinate Jacobians. Use the orientation
$dx^0\wedge dr\wedge\omega_{S^2}$.

For arbitrary $M,q_e,q_m\in\mathbb R$, put $Q^2=q_e^2+q_m^2$ and
$f(r)=1-2M/r+Q^2/r^2$. On every open $J\subset(0,\infty)$ with $f\ne0$, the
dyonic RN datum of [[def-emg-xs-rn-data]] is a geometric electrovac datum of
[[def-emg-xs-geometric-electrovac]] on
$\mathbb R_{x^0}\times J\times S^2$. In particular, its global two-form is
smooth, $d\mathcal F=d(\star_g\mathcal F)=0$, and
$\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}=2Q_{ab}(\mathcal F)$ everywhere on that domain.

derivations.claim: For $r>R_0>4M$, $f_\lambda(r)>1-2M/r>1/2$, so the metric is Lorentzian and the fixed exterior domain avoids every zero of $f_\lambda$. The parameter family is smooth on $(-\epsilon,\epsilon)\times U$ and is the $q_m=0$ Reissner–Nordström family of [F1]. By [F2], every member is an exact geometric electrovacuum on the same $U$.

Differentiating the displayed formulas gives $\dot f_0=2q_0\ell_*/r^2$,
$$h=-\dot f_0\,(dx^0)^2-f_0^{-2}\dot f_0\,dr^2,\qquad f=-\frac{\ell_*}{r^2}dx^0\wedge dr.$$
These tensors are smooth on $U$, independent of $x^0$, and $f\ne0$. By [F5] the pair solves the linearized equations.

For any $\lambda$, on the fixed exterior $f_\lambda>1/2$, so $g^{00}=-f_\lambda^{-1}$, $g^{rr}=f_\lambda$, and $|\det g|=r^4\sin^2\theta$. Hence $\mathrm{vol}_{g_\lambda}=r^2\sin\theta\,dx^0\wedge dr\wedge d\theta\wedge d\phi$. The two-form has $({\mathcal F_\lambda})_{0r}=-q(\lambda)/r^2$, so $({\mathcal F_\lambda})^{0r}=q(\lambda)/r^2$. Using the orientation in [F1] and the component Hodge formula [F4] gives $\star_{g_\lambda}\mathcal F_\lambda=q(\lambda)\sin\theta\,d\theta\wedge d\phi=q(\lambda)\omega_{S^2}$. The outward coordinate sphere has this positive area orientation, and direct integration in polar coordinates gives $\int_{S_r}\omega_{S^2}=\int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^\pi\sin\theta\,d\theta\,d\phi=4\pi$. By [F3], $q_e(S_r)=q(\lambda)$, so differentiating yields $\partial_\lambda q_e(S_r)|_0=\ell_*>0$. Since the nonzero component $f_{x^0r}=-\ell_*/r^2$ is independent of $x^0$, it cannot converge to zero as time tends to either infinity at any fixed $r>R_0$. This is a mathematical counterexample to universal componentwise decay without parameter-mode subtraction, not an assertion about physical observations or nonlinear stability.
